pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

22	## Design (settled)
23	
24	- **Delivery:** the room delivers every intel message kind to its recipients. `revealOf` grows into a full mapping, with rumors, sightings, stale notices and `no-lead` added.
25	- **Journal record (room-side):** intel's `IntelPlayerState.journal` keeps island and sector rumors with their status (active, stale, resolved), but not sightings or no-lead notices, and it doesn't link a stale rumor to what followed it. So the room keeps a per-player journal log (bounded to the last 24 entries), fed by every message the player receives. Each entry has the entry number, the kind (island or sector rumor, carrier sighting, no-lead), the type, the target name, the reason, the tick, and a status of active, stale or resolved (from `rumor-resolved` when the player gets the type). A stale entry is marked superseded by the next lead of the same type the player receives, whatever its reason: intel may give a `fresh` lead instead of a `replacement` when a loss and a stale rumor coincide, or deliver a deferred sighting later. The log is part of the player's private status, so a reconnecting player gets it back.
26	- **Journal:** **M** opens and closes the journal panel (readable DOM text). It shows your current rumors: the type, the island name or the sector name, and why you got it (start, fresh, targeted, replacement, sighting). Stale rumors are greyed out with their replacement. It also shows the islands you know, your collected types, and your kit with its §9 description. "Islands you know" means the islands you've had in sight or moored at. The room tracks them per player from the same sight filter the markers use, keeps each island's unlocked state as last seen, and adds whether you solved its ruin. A short toast announces each new lead.
27	- **Sectors on the sea:** faint 3 × 3 sector borders on the sea, with the sector's name shown when you enter it. The borders only show while the journal is open or a sector lead is active, so the sea stays clean.
28	- **Targeted rumor (one purchase per player per tick, charge only on delivery):** moored at any dock, the journal offers "Buy a rumor (25 gold)" for each type you're missing that has an available lead (`targetedRumorAvailability`). Types with free coverage show "covered" and can't be bought. The ledger has no refunds, so no gold may ever be taken for a rumor that isn't delivered. The room resolves requests like this:
29	  1. **Queue with limits:** requests arrive between ticks. A request whose (player, client id) is already pending is merged with it: it takes no slot, and both are answered by the one decision. The room keeps at most 2 pending requests per player; more are refused at once (`busy`) and nothing is kept. The button is disabled while one is pending.
30	  2. **Replay first:** a request whose (player, client request id) the room has already decided is answered from the room's record, before any check: a bought id resends its delivered lead (the ledger's `replayed`), and a refused id resends the same refusal. The room keeps every bought id and the last 16 refusals per player, like the ledger.
31	  3. **One per player per tick:** each world tick, the room takes **at most one** pending request per player, oldest first; the rest wait for a later tick. So the pre-check below can't be spent twice.
32	  4. **Where and what:** the whole purchase (checks, `stepIntel`, `purchase`) runs in the reveal step, immediately before and around `stepIntel`, after every other ledger operation of the tick (advance, encounters, channels, settlements, grants). The checks, in order: (a) the buyer's ship is **moored at a dock on this tick** (authoritative, not just the button; a request queued at a dock and processed after casting off is refused `not-at-dock`); (b) the ledger's state (in play, not in a duel or the theft window, not disconnected, at least 25 gold), read through the ledger's own exported queries, not copied rules; (c) `targetedRumorAvailability` for that type, which must offer a lead. Any failure gives a recorded refusal with its reason, no charge, and never reaches `stepIntel`.
33	  5. **`stepIntel`** with the request, under a room-namespaced intel id (`<playerId>:<clientRequestId>`, because intel's ids are global and the ledger's are per player).
34	  6. **Only if the intel outcome delivers a lead** does the room call the ledger's `purchase` with the client's id. Steps 3 and 4(a) on the same synchronous tick make its success an invariant: no other gold changes for that player between the check and the purchase. The room doesn't write a fallback branch for it. A refused purchase here means a bug, so it throws, and the match faults (§12), like any broken invariant in `worldTick`. An integration test sends bursts of requests for different types, across players and ticks, with gold between 25 and 49, and checks every delivered targeted lead is charged exactly once and every undelivered one isn't (`checkLedger` after every tick). Any intel outcome that doesn't deliver a lead goes through **one shared branch**: a recorded refusal carrying intel's reason, with no charge. The room doesn't branch per outcome. After the checks above, few such outcomes are reachable (for example a stale rumor or a snapshot boundary on the processing tick). Test the shared branch with a reachable case, which a test hook may set up.
35	
36	  Update the "Rumor flow" paragraph in `docs/objectives.md` (owned) and document the order in `docs/architecture.md`. `economy-online`'s dockside shop will later list the same purchase.
37	- **Keys:** **M** opens and closes the journal (the map and journal); Esc also closes it. M doesn't clash with E, R, F, J, U or I. Tab stays the browser's focus key: inside the open journal, Tab moves between its buttons, and Enter or Space activates one (§13 keyboard-navigable menus). The panel key rules apply: no key events are taken from text fields, and the helm stays live while the journal is open.
38	
39	## Acceptance
40	
41	Each item names the test that proves it. Integration tests use headless clients through the real room.
42	
43	1. **Start rumors** (integration): at control start every player gets a start rumor naming an island with a sealed source, or a sector with a cache, of a type they lack. It never names a carrier.
44	2. **Fresh and replacement leads** (integration): losing a type in a settled theft gives the loser a free fresh rumor. A journal rumor whose source gets collected goes stale and is replaced. Entering a duel isn't a loss.
45	3. **Targeted purchase** (integration):
46	   - buying with 25 gold delivers one targeted rumor and deducts 25;
47	   - a request refused by intel's step on the processing tick (the shared non-delivery branch) is charged nothing;
48	   - a request processed after the ship cast off is refused `not-at-dock` and charged nothing;
49	   - a retry of a still-pending id is merged and answered once;
50	   - two players using the same client request id are independent (the namespaced intel id);
51	   - two requests of different types in one tick from a player with 25–49 gold: one is delivered and charged, the other waits a tick and is then refused for gold, uncharged;

53	   - a third pending request is refused `busy`, and a request for a type with no available lead never reaches `stepIntel`;
54	   - a retry with the same request id is replayed without charging again;

- **Delivery:** the room delivers every intel message kind to its recipients. `revealOf` grows into a full mapping, with rumors, sightings, stale notices and `no-lead` added.
- **Journal record (room-side):** intel's `IntelPlayerState.journal` keeps island and sector rumors with their status (active, stale, resolved), but not sightings or no-lead notices, and it doesn't link a stale rumor to what followed it. So the room keeps a per-player journal log (bounded to the last 24 entries), fed by every message the player receives. Each entry has the entry number, the kind (island or sector rumor, carrier sighting, no-lead), the type, the target name, the reason, the tick, and a status of active, stale or resolved (from `rumor-resolved` when the player gets the type). A stale entry is marked superseded by the next lead of the same type the player receives, whatever its reason: intel may give a `fresh` lead instead of a `replacement` when a loss and a stale rumor coincide, or deliver a deferred sighting later. The log is part of the player's private status, so a reconnecting player gets it back.
- **Journal:** **M** opens and closes the journal panel (readable DOM text). It shows your current rumors: the type, the island name or the sector name, and why you got it (start, fresh, targeted, replacement, sighting). Stale rumors are greyed out with their replacement. It also shows the islands you know, your collected types, and your kit with its §9 description. "Islands you know" means the islands you've had in sight or moored at. The room tracks them per player from the same sight filter the markers use, keeps each island's unlocked state as last seen, and adds whether you solved its ruin. A short toast announces each new lead.
- **Sectors on the sea:** faint 3 × 3 sector borders on the sea, with the sector's name shown when you enter it. The borders only show while the journal is open or a sector lead is active, so the sea stays clean.
- **Targeted rumor (one purchase per player per tick, charge only on delivery):** moored at any dock, the journal offers "Buy a rumor (25 gold)" for each type you're missing that has an available lead (`targetedRumorAvailability`). Types with free coverage show "covered" and can't be bought. The ledger has no refunds, so no gold may ever be taken for a rumor that isn't delivered. The room resolves requests like this:
  1. **Queue with limits:** requests arrive between ticks. A request whose (player, client id) is already pending is merged with it: it takes no slot, and both are answered by the one decision. The room keeps at most 2 pending requests per player; more are refused at once (`busy`) and nothing is kept. The button is disabled while one is pending.
  2. **Replay first:** a request whose (player, client request id) the room has already decided is answered from the room's record, before any check: a bought id resends its delivered lead (the ledger's `replayed`), and a refused id resends the same refusal. The room keeps every bought id and the last 16 refusals per player, like the ledger.
  3. **One per player per tick:** each world tick, the room takes **at most one** pending request per player, oldest first; the rest wait for a later tick. So the pre-check below can't be spent twice.
  4. **Where and what:** the whole purchase (checks, `stepIntel`, `purchase`) runs in the reveal step, immediately before and around `stepIntel`, after every other ledger operation of the tick (advance, encounters, channels, settlements, grants). The checks, in order: (a) the buyer's ship is **moored at a dock on this tick** (authoritative, not just the button; a request queued at a dock and processed after casting off is refused `not-at-dock`); (b) the ledger's state (in play, not in a duel or the theft window, not disconnected, at least 25 gold), read through the ledger's own exported queries, not copied rules; (c) `targetedRumorAvailability` for that type, which must offer a lead. Any failure gives a recorded refusal with its reason, no charge, and never reaches `stepIntel`.
  5. **`stepIntel`** with the request, under a room-namespaced intel id (`<playerId>:<clientRequestId>`, because intel's ids are global and the ledger's are per player).
  6. **Only if the intel outcome delivers a lead** does the room call the ledger's `purchase` with the client's id. Steps 3 and 4(a) on the same synchronous tick make its success an invariant: no other gold changes for that player between the check and the purchase. The room doesn't write a fallback branch for it. A refused purchase here means a bug, so it throws, and the match faults (§12), like any broken invariant in `worldTick`. An integration test sends bursts of requests for different types, across players and ticks, with gold between 25 and 49, and checks every delivered targeted lead is charged exactly once and every undelivered one isn't (`checkLedger` after every tick). Any intel outcome that doesn't deliver a lead goes through **one shared branch**: a recorded refusal carrying intel's reason, with no charge. The room doesn't branch per outcome. After the checks above, few such outcomes are reachable (for example a stale rumor or a snapshot boundary on the processing tick). Test the shared branch with a reachable case, which a test hook may set up.

  Update the "Rumor flow" paragraph in `docs/objectives.md` (owned) and document the order in `docs/architecture.md`. `economy-online`'s dockside shop will later list the same purchase.
- **Keys:** **M** opens and closes the journal (the map and journal); Esc also closes it. M doesn't clash with E, R, F, J, U or I. Tab stays the browser's focus key: inside the open journal, Tab moves between its buttons, and Enter or Space activates one (§13 keyboard-navigable menus). The panel key rules apply: no key events are taken from text fields, and the helm stays live while the journal is open.

## Acceptance

Each item names the test that proves it. Integration tests use headless clients through the real room.

1. **Start rumors** (integration): at control start every player gets a start rumor naming an island with a sealed source, or a sector with a cache, of a type they lack. It never names a carrier.
2. **Fresh and replacement leads** (integration): losing a type in a settled theft gives the loser a free fresh rumor. A journal rumor whose source gets collected goes stale and is replaced. Entering a duel isn't a loss.
3. **Targeted purchase** (integration):
   - buying with 25 gold delivers one targeted rumor and deducts 25;
   - a request refused by intel's step on the processing tick (the shared non-delivery branch) is charged nothing;
   - a request processed after the ship cast off is refused `not-at-dock` and charged nothing;
   - a retry of a still-pending id is merged and answered once;
   - two players using the same client request id are independent (the namespaced intel id);
   - two requests of different types in one tick from a player with 25–49 gold: one is delivered and charged, the other waits a tick and is then refused for gold, uncharged;
   - a retried refused id gets the same refusal; a retried bought id is replayed even after the player's gold fell below 25 or while in a duel;
   - a third pending request is refused `busy`, and a request for a type with no available lead never reaches `stepIntel`;
   - a retry with the same request id is replayed without charging again;
   - a covered type is refused without charge, and so is a purchase with too little gold;
   - a purchase while in a duel is refused;
   - the gold identity holds (`checkLedger`).
4. **Sightings** (integration, with test-only short timings): when every copy of a missing type is carried by others, the lead is a carrier sighting delayed by the configured interval, at most one per player per snapshot. The slice has 4 copies per type and a player holds one of each type at most, so the test uses 5 headless players (4 carry the type, the 5th lacks it). Add a test-only `carrierInterval` timing, whose sighting delay equals it and whose carrier reveal is a multiple of it, so the intel validator accepts it.
5. **Hidden information on raw messages** (integration): across a scripted match that includes a duel, no frame to a player carries another player's rumor, journal entry, rubbing id, or a source's, cache's or unseen ship's position. Every intel-derived message goes only to its recipient. Ship ids for ships in sight, the grapple's ids and the results' ids are already public by design; they're allowed, and the test states that.
6. **Reconnect** (integration): a player who reconnects gets their journal back unchanged.
7. **UI** (web unit): the journal model (entries of every kind, stale and replaced links, reasons, islands, types, kit), the M and Esc keys, focus traversal inside the panel, the purchase button states (available, covered, too little gold, not at a dock), the toast, and the sector-border visibility rule.
8. **Browser scenario `rumor-journal`** (the policy's description of this scenario says "Tab"; the journal key is **M** per the design above, and the scenario id is unchanged):
   - two browsers start a private match;
   - the host opens the journal with M and reads its start rumor (a type and an island or sector name) from the page;
   - it sails to a dock, moors, buys a targeted rumor and sees its gold drop by 25 and a new journal entry marked "targeted";
   - the guest's page never shows the host's rumors.
9. **The existing scenarios still pass**, including the full match and the ruin, fruit and theft loops.
10. **Carried from `fruit-kits-online`'s approving reviews:**
    - the fruit panel stays open long enough to show the `reserved` and cast-off interruption reasons, which it closes too early to show today (a web unit test plus a room-level status test);
    - an auto-repeated F keydown (`event.repeat`) from the press that opened the panel never starts eating; only a fresh press does (web unit test);
    - `receiveOpenRuin` checks `island === null` before calling `openRuin`, matching its `island: number` type, instead of relying on the pure module's runtime check;
    - the fruit hidden-information test takes its marks before the players join, so it also covers the first syncs;
    - an integration test shows that a duel fought after a lost duel starts with the eater's kit (duel diagnostics or the lobby `kits`).
11. **The branch table:** `docs/intel-online-coverage.md` has one row for each room-level and UI branch this feature adds or changes: the file and function, the branch, and the test that fails when the branch is deleted.
    - Build it by deleting each branch on a scratch copy, running the deletions in parallel batches. Don't commit those edits.
    - A branch with no failing test gets a new test. A branch that can't change the outcome is marked `equivalent`, with a one-line reason. Dead code is removed.
    - There are no `unreachable` or `untested` rows, and the completion report's `untested` list is empty.
12. `docs/architecture.md` gains an "Intel in the room" section of at most half a page.
13. `npm ci` then each of the five policy checks passes from a clean checkout, with all browser scenarios. The integration suite stays well inside its time budget; report its duration.

Browser checks: each scenario id appears in exactly one test title as `[scenario:<id>]`. That test, when it passes, attaches exactly one image/png named `screenshot:<id>` (other attachments are fine). The verifier refuses anything else. Then check the report with the verifier's own rules: run the exact `check-report` command the controller appends to this task when it pins it.
